content.value_statement: Abrupt interface changes make buttons, notifications, and panels harder to follow. This skill guides functional CSS and React animations with reduced-motion support and visual checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide hover, press, and focus feedback with CSS transitions and Motion gesture props.
Provide enter and exit patterns for toasts, drawers, and panels using AnimatePresence or modern CSS.
Explain layout transitions, shared-element animation, and drag-to-reorder lists in React.
Provide CSS recipes for toggles, loading indicators, popovers, and animated custom properties.
Show reduced-motion guards with CSS media queries and Motion accessibility APIs.
Describe standalone HTML demos with deterministic states and local Playwright screenshot verification.
limitations: React animation examples require React and Motion; CDN-based standalone demos need network access.
Modern CSS features require browser compatibility checks and fallbacks for unsupported browsers.
Referenced screenshot helper scripts are not included in the supplied files.
Examples are instructional snippets, not complete production components or an automated accessibility test suite.

use_cases.title: Polish Interactive Product Controls
use_cases.description: Add consistent press feedback, animated toggles, and loading transitions to existing product interfaces.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interface Motion
use_cases.description: Create standalone HTML interaction demos with clear idle, active, and open states for visual review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Transitions
use_cases.description: Define reusable timing, exit behavior, focus feedback, and reduced-motion patterns for shared components.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Add Button Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Add CSS hover, press, and keyboard focus feedback to my button. Keep feedback fast and respect reduced-motion preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Animate a Drawer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone HTML drawer demo using modern CSS. Include open and closed states, reduced-motion support, and a fallback for unsupported browsers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prototype panel transitions without a build step.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Build a Toast Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate my React toast stack with Motion. Use stable keys, AnimatePresence, and layout transitions so dismissed toasts exit while remaining items reposition smoothly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate insertion, removal, and sibling movement.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Verify Shared-element Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a React gallery with shared-element thumbnail transitions. Include reduced-motion behavior and deterministic preview states. Use local screenshots to inspect settled states and distortion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop and visually verify coordinated layout transitions.

output_examples.input: Give a settings toggle clear motion without distracting users.
output: The toggle knob moves between its off and on positions with a short transition.
The track color reflects the selected state.
Reduced-motion users receive state feedback without large movement.

output_examples.input: Make dismissed notifications leave smoothly without holding empty space.
output: Each toast has a stable identity and an exit animation.
The toast stack uses layout transitions while dismissed items leave the layout flow.
Visual checks cover populated, dismissed, and empty states.

output_examples.input: Prepare a drawer interaction demo for visual review.
output: A single HTML demo provides closed and open drawer states.
A state query parameter selects the settled preview state.
Local screenshots support comparison across states and reduced-motion settings.

best_practices: Prefer transform and opacity for frequent motion, and keep most interaction transitions within 100 to 250 milliseconds.
Preserve keyboard focus feedback and provide reduced-motion alternatives for spatial animation.
Verify meaningful states with local screenshots, and check exit timing, layout distortion, and browser fallbacks.
anti_patterns: Do not add long decorative motion that delays routine interaction feedback.
Do not remove elements before exit animations finish or use unstable keys for animated lists.
Do not assume modern CSS support or ignore reduced-motion preferences.

faq.question: Does this skill require React?
faq.answer: No. CSS recipes work without React. Motion examples require React and the Motion library.

faq.question: What interactions does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers button feedback, toggles, toasts, drawers, list reordering, shared-element transitions, and loading states.

faq.question: Can I create a demo without a build tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes single HTML demos using CSS or CDN-loaded React and Motion. CDN imports require network access.

faq.question: How does it support reduced motion?
faq.answer: It provides CSS media queries, useReducedMotion examples, and MotionConfig guidance to reduce spatial movement while retaining feedback.

faq.question: Are screenshot tools included?
faq.answer: No helper scripts are included. The documentation provides a local Playwright screenshot command, which requires an available Playwright environment.

faq.question: Does it guarantee browser support or production readiness?
faq.answer: No. Check target browsers, add fallbacks, and test accessibility and performance before production use.
